patients.summary: Thirty-year-old administrative assistant who joins in July 2024 with right carpal tunnel syndrome, treated with a night splint. Her second pregnancy (2025-2026) is complicated by mild gestational hypertension at 35 weeks and ends in a precipitous term vaginal delivery after an ED presentation; the hypertension resolves postpartum.

events.reason: New patient; numbness and tingling right hand

procedures.procedure: Office visit, new patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 30 y/o F, admin assistant. Moving her care here; prior PCP and OB were at a group out of the area. Records release signed today.

CC: R hand numbness/tingling.

HPI: Started roughly six weeks ago. Thumb, index and middle finger on the right, pinky spared. Much worse at night; a couple of nights a week it wakes her up and she shakes the hand out. Notices it some days at the keyboard too. No injury, no fall on the hand, never had this before. No neck pain. Left hand fine.

PMH: nothing chronic. G1P1 - term vaginal delivery 2021, uncomplicated per pt.
PSH: none.
Meds: prenatal vitamin daily (she and her husband would like a second child in the next year or so and her OB had her start it).
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother had preeclampsia with one of her pregnancies and a very fast labor with another.
SH: admin assistant, mostly computer work. Never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: well appearing. Neck full ROM, Spurling negative. R wrist: no swelling, no redness or warmth. Tinel's positive at the R carpal tunnel. Phalen's brings on her tingling at about 30 sec. Thenar bulk normal. Grip and APB strength 5/5 bilaterally. Reflexes 2+ and symmetric at biceps, triceps, brachioradialis. Sensation otherwise intact. L wrist Tinel/Phalen negative. Heart regular, lungs clear.

A/P:
1. R carpal tunnel syndrome - classic hx and exam, no weakness or atrophy. Neutral-position wrist splint at night, try to keep the wrist straight at the keyboard (she's going to ask about a keyboard tray and wrist rest at work). Video f/u in about 2 months; if not better or any weakness, will talk about next steps.
2. Health maintenance - baseline CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH today; HIV and hep C screen offered and she accepts. Pap with HPV per prior records - will confirm when records come. PHQ-2 0.
3. Preconception - continue prenatal vitamin.

documents.title: Records Request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records request faxed to prior primary care and OB group with signed release. Requested last 5 years of office notes, labs, immunizations, Pap results and delivery summary.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Monica - all of your bloodwork from Monday came back normal: blood counts, kidney and liver tests, thyroid and cholesterol. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Nothing to change. Let me know how the splint is going.

reports.text: Specimen: cervical, liquid-based. Satisfactory for evaluation; transformation zone component present. Interpretation: negative for intraepithelial lesion or malignancy. High-risk HPV: not detected.

documents.title: Prior Practice Records
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Records received from prior primary care/OB group (48 pages), scanned to chart. Includes office notes 2019-2024, immunization record, Pap/HPV 09/2022, and labor and delivery summary from 2021. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed prior records. G1P1, SVD at term in 2021, uncomplicated pregnancy and delivery, normotensive throughout. Tdap given in that pregnancy (03/2021). COVID primary series 2021. Pap with HPV 09/2022 negative/negative - next due 2027. No chronic problems or meds other than prenatal vitamin. Immunization list updated.

documents.title: Splint question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, quick question. The splint is helping at night, I'm sleeping through most nights now. Should I be wearing it at work too? It makes typing kind of awkward. Thanks, Monica

documents.title: RE: Splint question
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Glad it's helping. Nights are the important part. During the day you don't need to wear it while typing - focus on keeping the wrist flat and taking short breaks. If you have a flare during the day, wearing it for a while is fine. We'll check in at the video visit in September.

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Video Visit - Carpal Tunnel Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit from her office, ID confirmed.

R CTS f/u. Wearing the splint nightly since July. Now only woken by it rarely, maybe once in a few weeks. Daytime tingling here and there on long typing days, settles when she shakes it out or takes a break. Work got her a keyboard tray. No weakness, not dropping things.

Obs on video: no distress, opposes thumb to each finger without difficulty, makes full fist.

A/P: R carpal tunnel syndrome, improving with conservative care. Keep the night splint, keep the ergonomic changes. Let me know if numbness becomes constant or any weakness. Flu shot this fall - nurse visit booked.

OBSTETRICS - NEW OBSTETRIC VISIT
Date of visit: 12/12/2025
Re: Monica Krause, DOB 02/10/1994
Referring: primary care

Thank you for referring Ms. Krause for her second pregnancy. G2P1001. LMP 10/17/2025, sure, regular. Today 8w0d by LMP; transvaginal ultrasound shows a single live IUP with CRL matching dates. EDD 07/24/2026.

OB hx: 2021 term SVD, uncomplicated, normotensive.
PMH: right carpal tunnel syndrome, managed with a night splint.
Meds: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with preeclampsia; mother with a precipitous labor.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol, admin assistant.

Exam: BP within normal limits. Heart and lungs normal. Abdomen soft. Pelvic deferred today; Pap current (2022, NILM/HPV negative).

Prenatal labs drawn today - see results.

Plan: continue prenatal vitamin. Routine prenatal care q4 weeks. Anatomy scan at 20 weeks. Given family history, will watch BP closely through the third trimester.

Attending obstetrician

Fetal anatomy survey complete and normal: head, face, spine, heart (four-chamber and outflow tracts), abdominal wall, stomach, kidneys, bladder, limbs. Placenta posterior, no previa. Amniotic fluid normal. Cervix long and closed.

documents.title: Obstetrics - Gestational Hypertension
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRICS - PRENATAL VISIT
Date: 06/19/2026, 35w0d
Re: Monica Krause, DOB 02/10/1994. cc: primary care

Routine visit. BP on arrival 142/92. Asymptomatic: no headache, no visual changes, no RUQ or epigastric pain. Good fetal movement. Kept in the office for observation and labs; repeat BP four hours later 140/90.

Urine protein/creatinine ratio 0.12. Platelets, creatinine, AST and ALT all normal.

Assessment: gestational hypertension, mild range, no proteinuria and no severe features. Her mother had preeclampsia.

Plan:
- Diet changes reviewed: less sodium and processed food, regular meals.
- Home BP cuff, check twice daily, call for 160/110 or higher, headache, vision change or RUQ pain.
- Weekly visits with BP and labs as needed.
- Delivery at 37 weeks: induction scheduled for 07/08/2026 (37w5d).
- Preeclampsia warning signs reviewed; she will go to labor and delivery with any of them, or with labor.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT RECORD
Date of service: 07/05/2026, arrival 06:20
Patient: Monica Krause, 32F

CC: contractions.

HPI: G2P1 at 37w2d (EDD 07/24) with regular contractions for about four hours, now every five minutes, along with low back pain. No vaginal bleeding. No fluid leaking. Pregnancy has been followed by her OB and is notable for mild gestational hypertension without proteinuria, which has been managed with diet. Induction had been planned for later this week. Also has a history of carpal tunnel syndrome. First pregnancy was uncomplicated with a term vaginal birth.

Meds: prenatal vitamin daily. Allergies: NKDA.
FH: mother with preeclampsia and a precipitous labor.
SH: never smoker, no alcohol, administrative assistant.

Vitals: BP 138/88, HR 88, T 37.1 C (98.8 F).

Exam: uncomfortable with contractions, otherwise well. Fundal height consistent with dates. Uterus irritable, contractions palpable about every 5 min. Fetal heart tones 140 bpm, 142 on recheck. Sterile speculum: cervical os closed, no blood, no pooling of fluid. No headache, no RUQ tenderness.

ED course: term labor in a patient with gestational hypertension. Discussed with OB on call; patient taken to labor and delivery by wheelchair at 07:05.

Disposition: L&D.
Emergency medicine physician

documents.title: Obstetric Discharge Summary
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
OBSTETRIC DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted 07/05/2026 07:05 from the emergency department. Discharged 07/07/2026.
Patient: Monica Krause, G2P2002

Admission diagnosis: term labor, 37w2d; gestational hypertension, mild, without proteinuria.
Discharge diagnoses: precipitous labor; spontaneous vaginal delivery at term; gestational hypertension.

Course: arrived on L&D contracting regularly. Cervical change was very rapid after arrival and she delivered a healthy infant by spontaneous vaginal delivery at 08:22, about two hours after she came into the ED. Labor was recorded as precipitous. Perineum intact. Placenta delivered spontaneously and complete. Blood loss within normal limits. GBS negative, no antibiotics needed. Infant went to the newborn nursery with routine care.

Postpartum: blood pressure highest 136/86, no antihypertensive needed. No headache or visual symptoms. Ambulating, voiding, tolerating diet. CBC on admission normal.

Discharge medications: prenatal vitamin daily.
Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up: BP check in one week (primary care has agreed to see her); postpartum visit with OB at 6 weeks. Return for BP 160/110 or higher, severe headache, vision change, chest pain, shortness of breath, heavy bleeding or fever.

Obstetrics

documents.title: Obstetrics - Postpartum Visit
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
POSTPARTUM VISIT 08/17/2026 (6 weeks)
Monica Krause, G2P2002, s/p precipitous SVD 07/05/2026 at 37w2d.

Recovering well. Bleeding stopped. Mood good; depression screening negative. Infant thriving.
BP 118/76. Home readings normal for several weeks.
Exam: abdomen soft, uterus involuted. Perineum healed, pelvic exam normal.

Assessment: normal postpartum course. Gestational hypertension resolved.
Plan: return to routine gynecologic care; Pap due 2027. History of gestational hypertension raises long-term cardiovascular risk - recommend yearly BP and periodic lipid screening with primary care.
